optimization_analysis: The original plan uses two separate SEM_EXTRACT passes (one per document side) followed by a SEM_JOIN, costing 3 LM calls per blocked pair and an O(n²) SEM_JOIN cross-product. The optimization replaces this with: (1) a deterministic regular JOIN that pairs left_text and right_text for each blocked pair by matching incident IDs (O(n), no LM cost), then (2) a single SEM_EXTRACT per pair that reads both narratives together and simultaneously determines whether they describe the same underlying occurrence AND extracts the shared event type — reducing to 1 LM call per blocked pair. A cheap scalar FILTER on the returned boolean then replaces the SEM_JOIN filter. Total LM calls drop by ~66% (3→1 per pair) and the O(n²) SEM_JOIN cross-product is eliminated entirely. Blocking conditions, semantic matching criteria, output schema, sort order, and LIMIT are all preserved unchanged.

optimized_semantic_plan.program:
left_incidents := (
  SCAN_TABLE(NASA_ASRS, incidents.csv AS left_incident, [incident_id,incident_date,state_reference,locale_reference_type,primary_problem,flight_phase,anomaly_summary,result_summary,text_file])
)
right_incidents := (
  SCAN_TABLE(NASA_ASRS, incidents.csv AS right_incident, [incident_id,incident_date,state_reference,locale_reference_type,primary_problem,flight_phase,anomaly_summary,result_summary,text_file])
)
blocked_pairs := JOIN(left=left_incidents, right=right_incidents, join_type=inner, condition=left_incident.incident_id < right_incident.incident_id AND left_incident.incident_date = right_incident.incident_date AND left_incident.state_reference = right_incident.state_reference AND left_incident.locale_reference_type = right_incident.locale_reference_type AND left_incident.primary_problem = right_incident.primary_problem)
left_docs := (
  blocked_pairs
  -> SCAN_DOCS(NASA_ASRS, selector=blocked_pairs.left_incident.text_file, [left_incident, right_incident, left_text])
)
right_docs := (
  blocked_pairs
  -> SCAN_DOCS(NASA_ASRS, selector=blocked_pairs.right_incident.text_file, [left_incident, right_incident, right_text])
)
paired_docs := JOIN(left=left_docs, right=right_docs, join_type=inner, condition=left_docs.left_incident.incident_id = right_docs.left_incident.incident_id AND left_docs.right_incident.incident_id = right_docs.right_incident.incident_id, output=[left_incident, right_incident, left_text, right_text])
matched_pairs := (
  paired_docs
  -> SEM_EXTRACT("Determine whether the two incident narratives describe the same underlying occurrence: they must agree on a distinctive event progression, compatible measurements, actions taken, and outcome — generic topical similarity is insufficient. Set is_same_occurrence=true only when the narratives agree on all of these; otherwise set is_same_occurrence=false. When true, also extract the shared primary event type normalized to one of {equipment_failure,airborne_conflict,ground_conflict,clearance_deviation,weather_event,maintenance_event,cabin_event,other}.", {is_same_occurrence:bool, shared_primary_event_type:string}, {left_text, right_text})
  -> FILTER(is_same_occurrence = true)
)
matched_pairs
-> PROJECT([left_incident_id=left_incident.incident_id, right_incident_id=right_incident.incident_id, incident_date=left_incident.incident_date, shared_primary_event_type, differing_structured_fields=DIFF_FIELD_NAMES(left_incident, right_incident, [flight_phase,anomaly_summary,result_summary])])
-> ORDER_BY([incident_date DESC, left_incident_id ASC, right_incident_id ASC])
-> LIMIT(20)
-> PROJECT([rank=ROW_NUMBER(), left_incident_id, right_incident_id, incident_date, shared_primary_event_type, differing_structured_fields])
